science.title: Copper derived from deep-sea hydrothermal vent minerals facilitates hydrogen cyanide formation from glycine in alkaline aqueous environment
science.description: In prevailing origin of life scenarios, hydrogen cyanide (HCN) is a key molecule for forming life’s essential building blocks, as demonstrated by HCN-centric prebiotic chemistry. However, whether HCN can be in-situ generated near deep-sea hydrothermal vents (HVs) has remained unexplored. Here, we show that a Cu-rich natural HV mineral reacts with glycine to generate HCN under alkaline, anaerobic conditions. Using 13C-isotopic labelled glycine, in-situ generation of HCN from glycine is confirmed, reaching concentration of 451.42 nM at 25 °C in 24 hours. HCN yield increases threefold at 10 °C. Copper leaching, and HCN generation from a glycine-CuCl2 mixture, or from synthetic Cu(Gly)2 in an anaerobic alkaline solution, indicate that copper(II) functions as an oxidant in this process. Because glycine can be generated through multiple pathways, our findings integrate cyanide chemistry into alkaline Cu-bearing HV environments, expanding the chemical diversity accessible within alkaline vent environments and potentially analogous systems beyond Earth.

science.title: Genome-resolved microbial communities across stratified freshwater lakes in Japan
science.description: Stratified freshwater lakes have vertically structured microbial communities with key roles in biogeochemical cycles. Despite the increasing availability of sequencing data, the number of standardized depth-paired datasets across lakes with different mixing regimes and trophic levels remain limited. Japan offers the opportunity to study lakes with diverse geological histories, trophic levels and mixing regimes within a relatively confined geographical region. Here we present a comparative metagenomic resource, which includes the four deep systems Lake Biwa, Lake Inawashiro, Lake Toya, and Lake Chuzenji. Eight metagenomic samples were collected in September 2022 from epilimnion and hypolimnion and were sequenced using both Illumina short-read and Nanopore long-read technologies. We recovered 569 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), including 204 high-quality genomes, 58 circular genomes, with 36.7% of all MAGs representing putative novel species. In addition to genomic data, this dataset includes physicochemical variables for the analyzed samples (e.g. oxygen saturation, temperature, pH, conductivity) as well as nutrient and organic carbon concentrations.
